fields.mechanism: Nano-architecture oxygen electrode characterized by high porosity and triple conductivity enhances interfacial stability and mass transfer through a self-assembly approach.
fields.intervention: Incorporate a high-porosity, triple-conductivity nano-architecture electrode layer using self-assembly to improve interfacial bonding and mitigate thermal stresses during cycling.
fields.expected_effect: Reduced cracking failure and enhanced stability over 1000 thermal cycles due to improved interfacial bonding and stress accommodation.
fields.falsification_test: Perform thermal cycle testing on cells with and without the nano-architecture electrode; compare crack initiation time and interfacial delamination area after 1000 cycles via scanning electron microscopy.

fields.mechanism: The mechanism involves enhanced interfacial stability and bonding at the electrode/electrolyte interface, facilitated by a self-assembled nano-architecture with high porosity and triple conductivity, which improves durability under thermal cycling.
fields.intervention: Implement a self-assembled nano-architecture oxygen electrode with high porosity and triple conductivity to improve interfacial bonding and mass transfer in the ceramic fuel cell.
fields.expected_effect: The cell will exhibit enhanced stability during thermal cycles, preventing cracking and extending lifespan to survive more than 1000 cycles.
fields.falsification_test: Perform thermal cycling tests up to 1000 cycles and measure the interfacial bond strength and crack propagation via post-mortem microscopy; if cracks appear before 1000 cycles or bond strength degrades significantly, the hypothesis is falsified.
fields.mechanism_source_span: enhanced interfacial bonding between the oxyge

fields.mechanism: Enhanced interfacial bonding and high porosity nano-architecture reduce stress concentration and improve mechanical compliance during thermal transients.
fields.intervention: Fabricate the ceramic fuel cell electrodes using a self-assembled nano-architecture with controlled high porosity and triple conductivity to maximize interfacial bonding strength between electrode and electrolyte layers, and use quantitative interfacial fracture toughness as the single microstructure measurement to predict 1000-cycle survival.
fields.expected_effect: The compliant, highly porous nano-architecture accommodates coefficient of thermal expansion mismatch strains during heating and cooling, while strong interfacial bonding prevents delamination initiation, enabling the cell to survive 1000 thermal cycles without cracking.
fields.falsification_test: Subject cells with varying measured interfacial fracture toughness values to 1000 thermal cycles between 200 °C and 600 °C; if cells with the highest interfacial toughness still exhibit crack densities statistically identical to baseline cells, the mechanism is falsified.
